USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Stopping maintenance treatment

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 35-year-old woman has remained seizure-free on levetiracetam and asks about stopping therapy. After assessing her recurrence risk, her neurologist determines that withdrawal is appropriate. Which strategy best limits the medication-withdrawal risk in this nonemergency setting?

  1. Abrupt discontinuation after the next dose
  2. Alternating full-dose days with untreated days
  3. Taking medication only when an aura occurs
  4. Replacing each dose with an over-the-counter sleep aid
  5. A supervised gradual taper
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

A supervised gradual taper

Gradual withdrawal helps limit increased seizure frequency and status epilepticus risk.

Understanding the options

A supervised gradual taper
Gradual withdrawal helps limit increased seizure frequency and status epilepticus risk.
Abrupt discontinuation after the next dose
Sudden withdrawal can increase seizure risk.
Alternating full-dose days with untreated days
Irregular exposure is not a planned gradual taper.
Taking medication only when an aura occurs
Maintenance therapy is not replaced by intermittent aura-triggered dosing.
Replacing each dose with an over-the-counter sleep aid
A sleep aid does not provide equivalent antiseizure protection.
